results.title: Expert-Recommended Diets for Diabetes | U.S. News
results.content:
### Key Takeaways

 A diabetes diet is a well-balanced diet meant to keep glucose levels within the normal range and consistent throughout the day, rather than swinging from highs to lows.
 Plan for regular, balanced meals to avoid high or low blood sugar levels.
 Include more whole grains, such as brown rice and oats.
 Make sure to eat non-starchy vegetables, such as broccoli and spinach.
 Limit added sugars and refined grains.

## Why Diet Matters in Diabetes Management [...] Here's the good news: a diabetes-friendly diet doesn't have to feel restrictive or dull. The trick is to focus on balance and make wise food swaps that support your goals.

 Choose whole grains and fiber-rich foods over refined carbs.
 Load up on non-starchy veggies.
 Add healthy fats.
 Go for lean proteins.
 Be mindful of carb choices and choose complex carbs over simple ones.

## Foods to Avoid

Let's face it – some foods aren't doing you any favors when managing diabetes. [...] Choosing whole foods, cutting back on added sugars and steering clear of refined carbs can help keep your blood sugar steady and reduce the risk of complications.

Managing diabetes isn't just about what you leave off your plate – it's also about what you put on it. Nutritious options like whole grains, lean proteins and healthy fats can make a real difference. Even minor, consistent tweaks to your eating habits can boost your energy and stabilize blood sugar.

## A Diabetes-Friendly Diet

results.title: Five Best Diets for Diabetes
results.content: For people living with diabetes, it’s important to eat in ways that help keep blood glucose levels within normal range consistently throughout the day, rather than rapidly fluctuating between figures that are high and low. This often translates to a focus on eating regular, portion-mindful meals that feature lean sources of protein and whole foods plentiful in fiber, along with limiting food or drinks that are high in sugar or simple carbohydrates. [...] Anderson-Haynes said the flexitarian diet may be a good option for people with diabetes. She pointed to a 2019 study showing that people who closely followed plant-based dietary patterns had a 13% lower risk of developing type 2 diabetes, compared to those who did not strictly follow a plant-based diet. [...] “Plant-based diets, such as the flexitarian diet, are plentiful in fiber, antioxidants, magnesium, and other nutrients that are well documented in research to assist with the prevention and management of chronic illness such as heart disease, cancer, and diabetes,” said Anderson-Haynes.
